newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Trade and Industry Bank posts profit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Trade and Industry Bank posts profit.

text.p: The private Bulgarian Trade and Industry Bank (BTIB) posted 1.2 billion levs pre-tax profit for 1996, from which it has set aside provisions of 1.19 billion levs, BTIB executive director said on Wednesday.
"The BTIB posted 1.2 billion levs pre-tax profit, set aside provisions of 1.19 billion levs and paid 3.5 million levs profit tax for 1996," Ognian Enchev told reporters.
The annual shareholders meeting decided that the bank's net profit of 7.1 million levs for 1996 will partly compensate some eight million levs losses suffered in 1994.

Bulgaria's private insurer Bulins and six foreign companies registered in Europe hold the majority stake of BTIB's 1.4 billion lev paid-in capital as of February 28, Enchev said. He declined to elaborate.
Bulins has acquired 14.3 percent of the bank's capital. The stake of the local private firm Nove Holding, one of BTIB's founders in 1994, has shrunk from 24.5 percent to 5.6 percent.
BTIB's assets totaled 5.2 billion levs on December 30, 1996. Its capital-to-risk-assets ratio at the moment stood at 8.77 percent.
"We expect further changes of the shareholders ratio after the current subscribtion for a new share issue is completed," Enchev said.
Last month the BTIB raised its share capital to 10 billion levs from current 1.4 billion levs through a new share issue. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
